subject: Co-sell eligibility and billing path for CloudPay purchase
messages:
From: Lily Zhao <lily.zhao@cloudpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial procurement constraints + marketplace question

Hi Vivek / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the model controls. Procurement has a few constraints that will change the path we take to purchase, and I wanted to surface them early so we can pick the right lane:

- We require a marketplace listing in our vendor catalog for any SaaS spend under $250k per year (for faster PO & approval).
- For larger multi-year commitments we need a signed MSA and prefer direct invoicing to our AP team.
- Co-sell incentives with cloud providers are a plus but not mandatory; procurement mainly cares about invoicing and tax paperwork.

Attached is the RFP and our standard supplier checklist. Can you outline the pros/cons for the two routes (marketplace private offer vs direct contract) specifically for:
1) Billing/invoice flow and timing
2) Eligibility for co-sell incentives (AWS/Azure/GCP)
3) Impact on implementation timeline and SSO/KMS onboarding

Would also appreciate a short mutual action plan we can include in our purchase request.

Thanks,
Lily Zhao
Head of IT Procurement
CloudPay

Attachments: CloudPay_RFP.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lily Zhao <lily.zhao@cloudpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial procurement constraints + marketplace question

Hi Lily — thanks for the clear note and the RFP. Quick summary up front: both paths are viable; the best choice depends on PO timing vs long-term contracting preferences. High-level differences below, followed by a recommended MAP you can paste into procurement.

Option A — Marketplace private offer (fast PO lane):
- Billing: Customer buys via the cloud marketplace private offer; provider (Redwood) receives payment through the marketplace and issues marketplace-native invoices. For AWS/Azure/GCP private offers we can accept PO numbers and the marketplace generally supports faster procurement flows.
- Co-sell: Eligibility for co-sell incentives requires listing + partner registration and in some cases a private offer acceptance window. Co-sell payouts/processes vary by provider and can lag invoice timing by 30–90 days.
- Implementation: Can be faster because the procurement sign-off is lighter, but note that KMS/HSM integrations and specific network/VPC requirements still require SSO and customer-side validation.

Option B — Direct contract (MSA + invoicing):
- Billing: Redwood invoices CloudPay directly; typically longer PO approval cycles for first-time vendors but gives you more control over payment terms and tax handling.
- Co-sell: We can still pursue co-sell if you allow partner referral, but certain provider incentives are tied to marketplace transactions.
- Implementation: Allows us to include detailed SOW, acceptance criteria, and bundled professional services on the contract.

Recommended mutual action plan (pasteable into your procurement request):
- Week 0–1: Decision on lane (Marketplace private offer vs Direct MSA).
- Week 1–2: If Marketplace: Redwood submits private offer to your cloud account owner. If Direct: Redwood submits draft MSA + SOW.
- Week 2–4: Procurement review, PO issuance or signature.
- Week 4–6: Security onboarding (SSO, KMS/HSM key exchange, account scoping) and test environment access.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx (high-level seat/usage estimate)

If helpful, we can run a short call with procurement/finance to walk the options and surface any idiosyncratic tax/SOW needs. Happy to join — propose Thu 11/11 or Mon 11/15.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Channel & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lily Zhao <lily.zhao@cloudpay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial procurement constraints + marketplace question

Lily — adding a few operational items and co-sell notes that typically come up: 

1) Marketplace listing & private offer mechanics (AWS/Azure/GCP):
- Private offer provides the cleanest PO-to-payment mapping for customers; we can create an offer SKU that matches your committed usage.
- For AWS: Must have vendor listing + consolidated billing alignment. For Azure: Marketplace private offers require MS marketplace publisher onboarding. For GCP: Marketplace procurement flows vary by reseller model.

2) Co-sell eligibility checklist (high level):
- Partner registration completed with the cloud provider (we can provide proof).
- Solution listed or private offer accepted in the provider console.
- Joint go-to-market approval if you plan to use provider co-sell credits.

3) Tax and resale considerations:
- If CloudPay requires a resale certificate, direct invoicing is cleaner; marketplace invoices often pass through cloud provider with their tax handling. Please confirm if a reseller/resale certificate is needed.

4) Attachments & evidence we can provide immediately:
- Redwood co-sell eligibility checklist (attached)
- Partner registration screenshots / partner ID (we can redact if needed)

Call-to-action: If you want the fastest procurement path and your AP team accepts marketplace invoices, go with Marketplace private offer. If your legal/tax/risk team insists on direct vendor invoices (or needs a signed MSA first), choose Direct MSA and we will accelerate the SOW to match your PO cadence.

Internal note: loop Marissa for billing ops once customer indicates lane.

Attachments: redwood_co_sell_eligibility_checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik
Dir., Strategic Accounts Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Lily Zhao <lily.zhao@cloudpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudpay.com>, Eric Wong <eric.wong@cloudpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T15:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial procurement constraints + marketplace question

Thanks both — this is very helpful. Procurement reviewed the notes and we have the following preference:

- For year one pilot (estimated spend ~$120k) we prefer the Marketplace private offer to accelerate PO issuance and get us into a sandbox faster.
- For any committed multi-year expansion we will transition to a Direct MSA so we can negotiate payment terms and include professional services.

Next steps for Marketplace private offer lane:
1) Redwood creates private offer and shares the private offer link + SKU mapping.
2) Redwood provides sample marketplace invoice flow and a point-of-contact in billing ops.
3) We will issue a PO referencing the private offer SKU once procurement confirms.

Can we target next Wed (11/10) for the private offer link and a brief 30-minute call to confirm the invoice fields our AP system needs? Please include Marissa from billing ops on the call.

On a separate note, procurement asked whether co-sell incentives would change the invoice flow — based on your notes we understand they do not block the marketplace purchase but may be processed separately. That's fine for now.

Thanks — will wait for the private offer link and invoice sample.

Best,
Lily
